title: Unattended stimuli are seen, not invisible

statements.text: The line between unconscious and conscious seeing lies between subjective invisibility and inattention. A stimulus missed for lack of attention is not truly invisible: it is seen but fails to be accessed and reported.

sources.quote: supporting the somewhat counterintuitive view that "invisibility" due to inattention is in fact not true invisibility, yet a case of failure to "internally report" or otherwise cognitively access and manipulate the information
